To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
deletion of the fab gene in E. facealis results in UFA auxotrophic and decreased release of proinflammatory cytokines.
the deletion of the fab N gene in Enterococcus results in an unsaturated fatty acid requirement, which can be compensated by supplementation with oleate.
the deletion of fabN in E. faecealis results in unsatured fatty acid auxotrohy and decreased cytokine release.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the type II fatty acid synthesis pathway in Gram-positive bacteria and its role in virulence.
the development of new antimicrobials against Gram-positive bacteria.
the development of a new approach to combat E. faecali infections by targeting the UFA synthesis pathway.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fabN gene is a potential drug target for antimicrobial treatment, but that the drug should be a UFA synthesis inhibitor rather than an inhibitor of FabN itself.
fabN is a target of choice for antimicrobial treatment in E. facealis only in combination with a fatty acid supplement.
the deletion of fabN in E. facealis results in an UFA auxotroph, but this phenotype can be rescued by the addition of oleic acid and human serum, which is in contrast to previous studies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the deletion of the fabA/B genes, which are essential for UFA synthesis in E. faecalis, would be a better target for antimicrobia...
deletion of the fabH gene in E. facealis is lethal and can not be rescued.
fabN is an interesting target for future research but is not an attractive target for antimicrobial development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
deletion of the fabH gene in the type II fatty acid biosynthesis pathway of E. faecals results in a decreased inflammatory cytokine response in vitro.
fabN is an essential gene for E. faecals and deletion of fabN results in unsaturated fat acid auxotrophy.
the deletion of fabN is a suitable tool to study the role of UFA synthesis in E. faecalis virulence and pathogenicity.
